description:
Storage defines one function twice under opposite `cfg` conditions and keeps stale `allow(dead_code)` attributes on public in-memory storage items.

## Background

`with_mutation_interruptions` exists as `#[cfg(feature = "test-support")] pub fn` (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:453-462`) and as `#[cfg(not(feature = "test-support"))] #[allow(dead_code)] pub(crate) fn` (`:473-482`). The self dev-dependency at `crates/jit/Cargo.toml:103` enables `test-support` for every test build, so the second form is never needed. Every source caller is `cfg(test)`, and one integration test calls it (`tests/cli_repo_workflow/profile_publication_tests.rs:113`).

`InMemoryStorage` and `InMemoryStorage::new` carry `allow(dead_code)` (`storage/memory.rs:34,68`). Both are public items of a public module (`storage/mod.rs:92`), so no lint fires without the attributes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `with_mutation_interruptions` in JSON storage has one definition, and storage holds no function or re-export defined twice under opposite `test` or `test-support` conditions.
- [hard] REQ-02: No public item in `storage/` carries `allow(dead_code)`.

## Notes

Platform-conditional implementations stay, such as `cfg(unix)` and `cfg(not(unix))` pairs (`storage/redo_apply.rs:283,471`, `atomic_write.rs:125`, `lock_cleanup.rs:40`, `repository_state_store.rs:1573,1989,2017,2148`, `redo_record.rs:368`). The `pub(crate)` configuration-dependent allows at `memory.rs:121,155,171` mark code that is live in other build configurations, and they stay too.
title: Remove cfg twins in storage
